rationale: This rule governs how any actor approaches any project, not one procedure's checkpoint; it holds regardless of which workflow or stage is running and rarely changes on its own, matching 6.1's own framing ('do not infer ownership from the current directory') more than a bounded procedure (6.2) or judgment scoped to one already-established checkpoint (6.4).

The coordinate-by-default / direct-mode-only-with-explicit-ask-and-single-owner rule is a standing precondition that shapes every task before any workflow begins; it has no trigger/bounded-outcome/completion shape of its own the way a workflow would, and it is a flat default rather than judgment an actor exercises at one particular checkpoint.

Dispatch mode has its own recognizable trigger (work spanning repositories, independent repo-owned sub-tasks, a need for isolated review, or an explicit worker request), a bounded outcome (one worker dispatched per owning repository), and a completion condition (progress monitored to reconciliation of merge order and cross-repo implications) — the defining shape of a reusable procedural outcome. It is not a standing rule true independent of a procedure's stage, and it is too coarse-grained (multiple steps, its own lifecycle) to be one checkpoint inside a larger procedure.

The default-branch prohibition and feature-branch requirement hold across every direct-mode implementation regardless of which stage of that work is underway; it is a flat, standing rule, not a bounded procedure with its own completion condition, and not a judgment exercised at one particular checkpoint.

PR-plus-required-CI-plus-review-plus-authorization-before-delivery is a standing completion criterion for all direct-mode work, independent of which specific implementation stage is running; it does not name its own trigger/outcome/completion the way a workflow would, and it is a fixed requirement rather than a judgment call exercised at one checkpoint.

This is a rule about how the instruction file itself must be authored, holding for every future edit regardless of any task's current stage — the clearest fit for a stable repository instruction surface rather than content scoped to one checkpoint.

Toolbelt-then-local-script-then-reported-manual-fallback governs any operation any actor performs, independent of which stage or workflow is running; unlike a helper it is not itself one deterministic operation but the standing precedence rule that decides which operation runs, so it stays at the invariant rung rather than becoming machinery subordinate to a checkpoint.
Trigger-gated skill loading applies to every session across every task — a standing discipline, not content scoped to one checkpoint's judgment.
Repository-local skill files taking precedence over any same-named registry skill is a standing resolution rule for every skill load, not a single checkpoint's judgment call.

Registry omission never blocking a skill, versus a genuinely missing or unreadable local file requiring a stop-and-report, is a standing rule governing skill resolution broadly across every task, not a bounded procedure or a single checkpoint's guidance.

Applying the reimplementation test: however sgt-context is implemented, 'load context and identify the owning repository or repositories, inherited instructions, paths, and cross-repo dependencies before selecting an execution mode' remains a meaningful boundary every task must cross before mode selection — a durable checkpoint operators would want tracked as entered, failed, or completed — not deterministic machinery subordinate to some other stage's outcome, and not itself a whole reusable procedure since it is one named step inside the larger standard task workflow.

Applying the reimplementation test: however sgt-td-list is implemented, 'check whether a canonical task already exists before creating a new one' remains a meaningful boundary — task creation genuinely branches on its outcome — so it earns its own checkpoint rather than being folded as judgment content into an adjacent stage, and it is too narrow and mechanical on its own to be a reusable workflow.

Applying the reimplementation test: regardless of what replaces sgt-watch --sync-all, 'reconcile active workers, branches, worktrees, retained gates, and handoffs before starting new work' remains a boundary operators would want measured — did reconciliation find something to resume, or not — a checkpoint, not merely a helper's deterministic step subordinate to another checkpoint's outcome.

This is guidance for the judgment already exercised at whichever checkpoint a scope- or risk-changing decision surfaces during — deciding whether a given unresolved point clears the ask-the-user bar — rather than a new boundary of its own; it has no independent entry, outcome, or completion condition the way the load-context or check-queue steps do, so it stops at 6.4's judgment-content representation.

Requiring recent meaningful events or a verified pane identity, and falling back to bounded one-shot checks when managed background execution is unavailable, is judgment about how to interpret ongoing monitoring evidence rather than a bounded checkpoint with its own entry and exit — it attaches to whichever dispatch/monitoring stage is already running instead of establishing a new one.

Applying the reimplementation test: whatever tool runs cleanup, 'run cleanup only after terminal state and preserved evidence are verified, as the final reconcile-and-deliver step' remains the meaningful closing boundary of the standard task workflow — cleanup running early is exactly the kind of failure worth tracking independently — so it is a checkpoint rather than judgment folded into an earlier stage.

Nonterminal-state handling — wake versus respond as the two resumption channels, never cleaning a waiting worktree, never rewriting an expected blocked exit as orphaned — is a standing lifecycle rule that applies to every worker in every workflow, not deterministic machinery of one script and not guidance scoped to a single checkpoint.

One canonical intent revision governing every dispatched implementation, review, PR, successor, recovery, and gate — plus gate-ownership resting solely with the coordinator, never a worker or remediation loop — is a cross-cutting consistency rule spanning the whole task, not one script's deterministic behavior nor one checkpoint's judgment.

Applying the reimplementation test: whatever tool provides it, 'the single validation-only boundary, launched once readiness is reached, with rereview required after any HEAD-changing remediation but without retriggering the full cycle' remains a meaningful checkpoint the standard workflow passes through exactly once — durable and measurable, distinct from ordinary monitoring — so it earns its own checkpoint rather than being folded into monitor-progress's judgment content.

Correcting stale in_progress bookkeeping the moment reality diverges is a standing truthfulness rule for task-tracker and fleet state, applicable regardless of which workflow or stage produced the divergence.

Never letting tool absence produce a silent skip, false success, or indefinite wait is a standing rule for any actor session, independent of which specific script or stage encounters the missing tool.

sgt-dispatch's agent-registry and interactive-only checks are deterministic gatekeeping run before any worker state is created — machinery crossing the dispatch checkpoint, not the checkpoint itself — and dispatch is invoked identically (same inputs, same rejection contract) whether triggered interactively or by the DAG hook, so it is shared rather than owned by one workflow.

Model-tuple precedence resolution and the unpinned-recording requirement are deterministic logic dispatch performs before any state exists; the same precedence and recording contract applies wherever sgt-dispatch is called, so it is shared machinery rather than one workflow's private helper.

The busy:true / busy:null (never busy:false) computation is a deterministic evaluation the snapshot command performs on every call; any caller — coordinator, bridge, or another workflow — gets the identical triple-verification contract, so it is shared rather than scoped to one workflow's checkpoint.

Model-tuple charset validation is a deterministic accept/reject check applied uniformly to every tuple dispatch or its config resolves, regardless of which workflow supplied it, so it is shared machinery rather than a single workflow's private helper or a judgment call.

launch_state/variant_verified honesty bookkeeping is deterministic evidence-recording performed identically by every dispatch, not a judgment an actor exercises at a checkpoint, and its contract — never overstate confirmation — is the same regardless of which workflow dispatched the worker.

Pane-identity verification against the live tmux server, plus display-only handling of managed-pane content, is deterministic safety machinery every dispatch path goes through identically; it prevents an injected notification from becoming a command regardless of which workflow is dispatching, so it is shared rather than workflow-local.

Choosing not to auto-approve and reserving --skip for stages already proven irrelevant is judgment the coordinator exercises at the moment it starts a shipping-gate run — it does not itself establish a new checkpoint (the run's own boundary already exists), so it is guidance that belongs in that stage's own context rather than a checkpoint in its own right or a script's fixed internal validation.

Which actor is permitted to start a no-mistakes run, and when, is a judgment applied at the run-starting checkpoint (has the branch been committed, is native validation done) rather than a new checkpoint of its own or a fixed script-internal rule, so it belongs in that stage's context.

Handling an ask-user gate — relay to the user and wait, never resolve it autonomously — is judgment the coordinator exercises while driving an already-established gate-run checkpoint, not a boundary with its own entry and exit.

The don't-edit / don't-abort-to-escape / preserve-all-commits discipline while a run is active is behavior the coordinator must exercise throughout the already-established gate-run checkpoint, not a new checkpoint or a script's internal deterministic logic.

Stopping active involvement at checks-passed rather than polling toward merge is a judgment about when the coordinator's own driving ends within the gate-run checkpoint, not a new boundary — the run itself continues monitoring in the background regardless.

Selecting a recovery action from the reported branch_sync state, and refusing to improvise git surgery around it, is judgment applied once a gate run has already failed or been cancelled — it reacts to that checkpoint's outcome rather than establishing a new one.

Treating the gate run as validation-only and routing findings elsewhere rather than fixing them inline is a constraint on what the coordinator does at the gate-run checkpoint, not a new checkpoint, and it is a disposition judgment rather than the router's own deterministic internals (dedup, severity normalization, digesting), which the adjacent findings-router units cover separately.

Barring correctness/security/data-integrity/test findings from defer-or-ignore, and never carding cosmetic/evidence-only findings, is a deterministic disposition rule sgt-no-mistakes-finding applies to every finding regardless of which workflow's gate run produced it, not a judgment the coordinator exercises case by case.

One shared axis definition driving both what a generated brief demands and what the findings router accepts is deterministic machinery ensuring the two never drift apart, applied identically to every worker brief regardless of which workflow dispatched it.

Normalizing reviewer severity spellings to a canonical error/warning/info set is a deterministic transformation the router applies to every finding it receives, independent of which workflow's review produced it — the icm-ladder's own 'normalizing JSON' example for this rung.

Digest-verifying a stored finding card and preserving a superseded revision on divergence is deterministic integrity machinery the router runs on every route, regardless of which workflow's finding is being updated, not a checkpoint or a coordinator's judgment call.

Post-redaction-only retention plus refusing to overwrite an unretried artifact is deterministic machinery governing every findings-route retry uniformly, independent of which workflow's gate run is being retried.

Hard-link-based admission locking, with fail-closed behavior when the filesystem doesn't support it, is deterministic locking machinery every dispatch and respond invocation goes through identically before proceeding, regardless of which workflow triggered them.

Applying the reimplementation test: whatever creates the isolated checkout, writes the brief, and starts the agent, 'a worker for this repo now exists and is running' remains the meaningful boundary dispatch-mode's later steps (monitor, reconcile) depend on — a checkpoint operators track per repo, not deterministic machinery subordinate to some other checkpoint's outcome; it is also too concrete a single event to be its own reusable workflow the way 'dispatch mode' as a whole is.

--adopt-branch's non-destructive resume behavior is one deterministic option of the shared dispatch mechanism, invoked with the same contract whether the caller is an interactive dispatch or a DAG-triggered one.

Sourcing the brief and context from a task-tracker task instead of an inline string is a deterministic input-resolution option of the shared dispatch mechanism, not specific to one workflow's checkpoint.
Enforcing declared cross-repo dependency ordering is deterministic sequencing machinery dispatch performs identically regardless of which workflow supplied the --deps ordering.

The --model > SERGEANT_MODEL > harness-default precedence is the same deterministic resolution rule applied by every dispatch invocation, restating the model-resolution contract at the option-doc layer rather than a workflow-specific judgment.

Verifying an explicitly-bound coordinator pane against the live tmux server before use is deterministic safety machinery every dispatch invocation performs identically, independent of caller workflow.

Requiring the origin profile and correlation id together is a deterministic argument-pairing validation dispatch performs the same way regardless of which workflow is dispatching with a callback origin.
Delegating origin validation to sgt-callback once both fields are present is deterministic machinery invoked identically by every dispatch that supplies callback origin data.
Dry-run's guarantee of creating nothing, including tmux state, is deterministic behavior of one dispatch flag, applied the same way regardless of which workflow is previewing a dispatch.

Refusing a fresh branch over unpushed prior commits, and pointing at --adopt-branch instead, is a deterministic guard dispatch applies uniformly before creating any branch, independent of caller workflow.

Requiring DAGR_RUN_ID/DAGR_STAGE_ID before proceeding is a deterministic precondition the DAG dispatch hook enforces identically for every DAG stage that becomes ready, regardless of which project's DAG is running.

Writing DAG run/stage tracking files into each dispatched repo's fleet state is deterministic bookkeeping the hook performs the same way for any DAG-triggered dispatch, so later watch/advance logic can find it.
Warning rather than failing when no fleet task ID can be extracted is deterministic, uniform error-handling in the DAG dispatch hook, not a judgment varying by workflow.
Reading the dag: block from the project's own YAML as the single source for the stage graph is deterministic config-sourcing machinery, applied the same way for every project's DAG run.
Preferring a stage's task-tracker task over its inline brief is deterministic precedence resolution dag-run applies identically to every stage regardless of which project's DAG is starting.

Registering declared stage dependencies with the external dagr engine is deterministic wiring dag-run performs the same way for every DAG stage; the ordering guarantee is already delivered by dagr's own gating rather than requiring a new capability from whatever engine hosts the workflow, so engine-gap was considered and rejected as premature — a working lower-rung mechanism already exists.
Reporting what would be registered without registering anything is deterministic, uniform dry-run behavior of dag-run, independent of which project's DAG is being previewed.
Failing fast on a missing dagr/yq dependency with an install pointer, before any other work happens, is a deterministic precondition check dag-run applies the same way to every invocation.

Rejecting empty/dot/absolute/slash-containing task ids before touching fleet state is a deterministic input-validation guard cleanup applies identically regardless of which workflow's task is being cleaned up.
Rejecting a symlinked or non-canonical task directory is a deterministic path-safety guard cleanup applies the same way to every task, independent of caller workflow.
Treating an already-removed task directory as success rather than error is deterministic idempotency behavior of cleanup, applied uniformly regardless of which workflow's task is being cleaned.

Syncing pending callback state before removing worktrees, and requiring full acknowledgement for whole-task cleanup, is deterministic machinery cleanup performs the same way whenever a task carries recorded callback origin state.

The same-filesystem requirement is a deterministic precondition enabling cleanup's atomic evidence-preservation step; the capability it enables is implemented today, not merely desired, so it does not meet the last-rung bar of a genuinely unrepresentable behavior — engine-gap was considered and rejected since a working, if filesystem-constrained, mechanism already exists.

Refusing new pane starts during a drain while storing responses generation-safely is deterministic admission-control machinery every relaunch/recovery path checks identically, regardless of which workflow's worker is affected.
Rejecting a combined project-plus-global drain scope is a deterministic argument-validation guard applied the same way on every drain invocation.
Restricting --wait to drain-setting mode, and --timeout to accompany --wait, is deterministic option validation applied uniformly by sgt-drain.
Activating the drain before waiting begins is a deterministic ordering guarantee the wait implementation enforces the same way every time, not a judgment call.

Treating an unconfirmable worker identity as unresolved rather than finished is a deterministic evaluation rule the drain wait applies to every worker uniformly; the underlying capability — provable liveness — is already achieved today through process-identity checks, so engine-gap was considered and rejected as unearned.
Leaving the drain active, naming unresolved workers, and terminating none of them on timeout is deterministic, uniform timeout-handling in the wait implementation.
Enforcing the project-name pattern and rejecting collisions with lock-artifact filenames is a deterministic validation guard applied identically to every drain/undrain invocation.
Requiring an already-active matching drain before force-stop proceeds is a deterministic precondition guard, applied the same way regardless of which workflow's workers would be targeted.
Requiring --yes or --dry-run before any worker is stopped is a deterministic confirmation guard sgt-drain-force applies uniformly.
Idempotent success when undraining an already-undrained scope is deterministic, uniform behavior of sgt-undrain.
Rejecting a combined --global and named-project undrain is a deterministic argument-validation guard applied the same way on every undrain invocation.

Gating recovery on both an in_progress status and a recorded stall diagnostic is a deterministic precondition check sgt-recover applies identically to every stalled worker, independent of caller workflow.
Escalating a second recovery attempt to needs_input instead of retrying is deterministic, uniform state-machine logic in sgt-recover, not a judgment exercised per workflow.
Killing the original pane only after the replacement is launched and validated is a deterministic ordering guarantee sgt-recover enforces the same way on every recovery attempt.
Refusing recovery when the recorded worktree is missing or unrecorded is a deterministic precondition guard applied uniformly by sgt-recover.

Restricting response delivery to needs_input/blocked/waiting/orphaned statuses is a deterministic status guard sgt-respond applies identically to every delivery attempt, regardless of which workflow's worker is waiting.

Refusing delivery when the recorded worktree can't be reconfirmed as an owned checkout, absent legacy migration recovery, is a deterministic verification guard applied uniformly; the underlying capability — provable ownership — is already met by existing checks, so engine-gap was considered and rejected.

Refusing delivery on an intent-revision mismatch is a deterministic verification guard sgt-respond applies the same way to every response, though the resulting requirement for an audited human decision is itself judgment exercised by whoever resolves the mismatch — the guard itself, not that downstream judgment, is what this record classifies.
Refusing to redeliver a still-pending response absent an armed escalation is a deterministic duplicate-delivery guard applied identically by sgt-respond regardless of caller workflow.

Escalating an unacknowledged durable delivery to a bounded relaunch on command re-run is deterministic recovery machinery built into sgt-respond itself, not guidance the coordinator separately exercises.
Rejecting an empty response before any delivery work begins is a deterministic input-validation guard applied uniformly by sgt-respond.
Refusing acknowledgement from a pane other than the one dispatch recorded as owning the worker is a deterministic identity-verification guard sgt-ack-response applies the same way every time.

Requiring the worker's own post-application proof to agree with the pending response before acknowledging is a deterministic verification guard, not a judgment call, applied identically regardless of caller workflow.
Requiring a non-empty result for done, or a nonblank reason for failed, is a deterministic proof-content guard sgt-ack-response applies uniformly.
Requiring the gate generation to have strictly advanced before acknowledging needs_input/blocked is a deterministic proof-freshness guard applied the same way to every acknowledgement.

Archiving the response and its proof before clearing pending files is a deterministic durability ordering sgt-ack-response enforces uniformly; the durable-record capability it provides already exists via this archive step, so engine-gap was considered and rejected as already met at this rung.
Grace-period-based stall detection and diagnostic-writing is deterministic monitoring machinery sgt-watch applies the same way to every live in_progress worker, independent of caller workflow.
Clearing a stale stall diagnostic once progress resumes is deterministic, uniform bookkeeping in sgt-watch, not a judgment call.
Reporting a terminal outcome back to the DAG engine when tracking files are present is deterministic integration machinery sgt-watch runs identically for every DAG-tracked repo.
Recycling a pane at most once per recorded identity is a deterministic idempotency guard sgt-watch applies uniformly, regardless of which workflow's worker owns the pane.

The read-only snapshot mode is deterministic, side-effect-free query machinery distinct from watch's human-oriented listing and lifecycle-mutating sync modes, offered identically to any coordinator or bridge that needs it rather than being a bounded, multi-step, outcome-producing procedure of its own.

Evaluating a wake condition through a read-only adapter keyed on its declared kind is deterministic machinery sgt-wake applies the same way to every waiting worker regardless of which workflow parked it there.
Failing terminally once a wake condition's deadline passes is deterministic, uniform timeout handling in sgt-wake.
Escalating to needs_input once max_attempts is exceeded is deterministic, uniform retry-bound handling in sgt-wake.
Immediately routing a human_response condition to needs_input without attempting automated evaluation is deterministic, uniform dispatch-by-kind logic in sgt-wake.

Strict allowlisting of wake-condition field names and value characters is a deterministic input-safety guard sgt-wake applies identically to every condition it reads, regardless of which workflow wrote it.
Validating the harness against the accepted registry before any model resolution or state-writing is a deterministic precondition guard sgt-interactive-worker applies uniformly on startup.
Requiring both an available worktree and an actual attached terminal is a deterministic startup guard applied the same way to every interactive worker launch.

Settling the handoff durably before publishing drained status is a deterministic ordering guarantee sgt-interactive-worker enforces uniformly on every cooperative drain; the durable-settlement capability it needs already exists via this ordering, so engine-gap was considered and rejected as already met.
Never fabricating a result and always removing a stale one on drain is deterministic, uniform status-honesty behavior in sgt-interactive-worker.
Checking only the global drain and the worker's own recorded project drain is deterministic scoping logic applied identically by every worker.

Classifying a notify message into completion/escalation/update from its leading text is a deterministic transformation sgt-notify applies the same way to every worker update, regardless of which workflow produced it.

Defaulting to a durable metadata-only wake marker rather than raw tmux injection is deterministic, uniform default transport behavior in sgt-notify, with raw injection available only as an explicit opt-in.

Deriving durable callbacks from authoritative task state rather than the free-text notify message is a deterministic integrity rule sgt-notify enforces uniformly, independent of which workflow's worker is calling it.
Completing other recording and deferring only the callback failure to the end is deterministic, uniform error-sequencing behavior in sgt-notify, applied the same way on every callback-sync failure.
